formationLabel: Lithuanian Catholics petitioned to break ground for a chapel June 21, 1947 · Immaculate Heart of Mary mission church established in 1948 · dependent on Sacred Heart, New Philadelphia · closure date unresolved
currentUse: Immaculate Heart of Mary was a Lithuanian Catholic mission and chapel in Middleport, dependent on Sacred Heart in New Philadelphia; it was not a separately erected Lithuanian parish. The mission is closed, but its exact terminal date and the chapel building's present condition or use remain unresolved. Four stained-glass windows are now in All Saints Chapel at St. Joseph the Worker in Orefield, and the former sanctuary's main altar and pulpit were installed in Blessed Teresa of Calcutta Church in Limerick. No exact Middleport street address has been established.
summary: Middleport's Lithuanian Catholic record represents Immaculate Heart of Mary mission and its chapel, not an independent parish. A June 21, 1947 archival index entry records the Lithuanian Catholic people of Middleport asking Cardinal Dennis Dougherty for permission to break ground for a chapel. A Schuylkill County Catholic church list dates Immaculate Heart of Mary to 1948 and identifies it as a mission of Sacred Heart, New Philadelphia. Field documentation likewise says Lithuanians built the church in 1948 but no new Lithuanian parish was created and priests came from New Philadelphia. The mission later closed; its exact end date, sacramental-record custody, street address, and building fate remain unresolved, although windows, altar, and pulpit from the church have documented later homes.

institutionLifecycle.currentVerification: Current first-party Catholic evidence identifies four Middleport stained-glass windows in St. Joseph the Worker's All Saints Chapel. These artifact transfers do not establish the present condition of the Middleport chapel.

historicalNarrative.text: A Lithuanian Catholic worshipping community existed in Middleport before the church was built. The Cardinal Dougherty correspondence index records a June 21, 1947 letter from the Lithuanian Catholic people of Middleport asking permission to break ground for a chapel. The entry proves a community and chapel petition, not an independently erected parish.

historicalNarrative.text: Immaculate Heart of Mary is dated to 1948 in a Schuylkill County Catholic church compilation. The entry appears under Missions and closed churches and expressly calls Middleport a mission of Sacred Heart in New Philadelphia. This directly contradicts treating the Middleport body as a separately countable parish.

historicalNarrative.text: Field documentation supplies the same institutional boundary from a different source. It says Middleport Lithuanians built an entirely new church in 1948, but that no new Lithuanian parish was created; priests came from New Philadelphia to celebrate Mass. The local institution is therefore described as a dependent mission with a chapel, while Sacred Heart remains a distinct institution.

historicalNarrative.text: The Middleport mission later closed, but the available sources do not supply a final Mass, suppression decree, or terminal year. Field documentation calls the church closed; a current Catholic chapel history says stained-glass windows from Immaculate Heart of Mary were received among artifacts from diocesan churches undergoing mergers or closings. Neither source establishes the former building's present condition.

historicalNarrative.text: Several sacred furnishings survived outside Middleport. St. Joseph the Worker identifies four Middleport stained-glass windows in its All Saints Chapel in Orefield. A 2012 Catholic news report says the main altar and pulpit from Immaculate Heart of Mary were installed in the new Blessed Teresa of Calcutta Church in Limerick. These transfers document artifact continuity, not institutional succession and not the fate of the chapel structure.

A questionable older address points instead to New Philadelphia, and Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary on Kaska Street is a distinct Ukrainian Catholic institution with a different history. Neither location is assigned to Immaculate Heart of Mary without direct site evidence.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The inherited `parish` classification conflicts with the 1947 chapel petition, the 1948 mission listing, and the field account stating that no new Lithuanian parish was created and priests came from New Philadelphia. The evidence supports reclassification to a Roman Catholic mission while retaining the same public route and canonical institution identity. The uncertain New Philadelphia address and Kaska Street Ukrainian Catholic church are excluded from the Middleport site record.
gaps: A mission-establishment or chapel-approval document beyond the correspondence index, exact canonical dependency instrument, exact street address and parcel, blessing or first-Mass date, last Mass and closure decree, sacramental-record custody, complete clergy history, cemetery, building ownership and present physical condition or use, and dates of furnishing removal remain unresolved.
